Subject: DPA / MSA redlines — SCCs & transfer-impact addendum for Knox Health

Hi Morgan —

Thanks again for the productive call last week. Attached are the current redlines from our side: a consolidated MSA with order form annotations (redlined-msa_knox_v3.docx) and a proposed DPA (dpa-proposal-knox-20250609.pdf).

Two items I want to call out up front so we’re all aligned:
- SCCs: we’ve inserted the standard EU SCCs (2021) and flagged the places where the Controller/Processor roles need overlap language to match Knox’s draft.
- Transfer impact addendum: because you referenced on-prem analytics jobs in EMEA, we’ve proposed a short transfer-impact addendum that limits cross-border exporting of EEA-origin data unless the specific dataset is scoped and agreed. This is intended to give you tighter controls without blocking our hosted inference offering.

Can you confirm whether Knox will accept the SCCs as-is and whether the proposed narrow transfer addendum is acceptable in principle? If there are commercial triggers tied to the wording, please flag those so I can elevate to pricing.

I’ve cc’d Laura (legal) for a quick review and Neha (privacy) for the transfer /tech-evidence items if we need a TIA.

Attachments: redlined-msa_knox_v3.docx; dpa-proposal-knox-20250609.pdf

Best,

From: Morgan Ellis <morgan.ellis@knoxhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Knox Health Legal <legal@knoxhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 16:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA / MSA redlines — SCCs & transfer-impact addendum for Knox Health

Jordan —

Thanks for sending these through. We reviewed with legal and have a few initial observations (attached: Knox_DPA_redlines.docx):

1) KMS / encryption at rest: we need assurance that keys for Knox EEA data can be customer-managed or that Redwood will guarantee that keys are region-bound. If not customer-managed, then we need an explicit statement about access controls and access logs.
2) Subprocessor carveouts: your DPA proposes broad subprocessor rights. Please narrow to named subprocessors for any production environment that will process EEA personal data, and add an approval step for new subprocessors affecting EEA workloads.
3) Transfer-impact addendum: the language in the addendum is close, but we need a stronger commitment that Redwood will not export EEA-origin datasets used for model tuning or analytics without explicit, prior written consent.
4) SCCs: legal prefers the Controller/Processor column mapping to mirror our internal catalogue; can you provide a short role matrix (which parties are controller/processor per module)?

We are okay to proceed on timeline if we can close the KMS and subprocessor points within the week. Sending our redline as tracked changes.

Cheers,
Morgan Ellis
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Knox Health
morgan.ellis@knoxhealth.com
(212) 555-0199

Attachments: Knox_DPA_redlines.docx

Team —

Forwarding Morgan’s redline. TL;DR of what Knox needs and proposed owners:

- KMS / encryption at rest: Morgan asks for customer-managed keys or a region-bound key guarantee + access logs. Owner: Neha (privacy) to confirm KMS options and engineering constraints.
- Subprocessor carveouts: narrow list of named subprocessors + approval step for EEA-impacting subprocessors. Owner: Laura (legal) to propose acceptable carve wording and a process for approvals.
- Transfer-export for tuning/analytics: knock-out ask — no export without explicit prior written consent if dataset originates in EEA. Owner: Laura + Neha to draft strengthened addendum wording.
- Controller/Processor role matrix: Morgan wants a short matrix mapping modules (hosting, logging, telemetry, model tuning) to roles. Owner: Ben to gather from solutions/infra and return a 1-pager.

Proposed timeline: engineer/legal answers on KMS + subprocessors by EOD Thurs (2025-06-12), updated redline back to Knox EOD Fri (2025-06-13). If we can’t meet that, I'll raise to pricing/leadership for timeline relief.

Morgan — cc’ing so you can see owners and timeline. Neha and Laura, if you want a sync before Thurs let me know and I’ll schedule a 30-min slot.

Thanks,
Jordan
